current_answer: Current evidence supports four separate choices: fal H3 Max Director is a finite hosted, context-carrying WebRTC session; Reactor FastH3 can run a chat-driven queue and paced RTMP broadcast but uses independently generated clips with hard cuts; FastVideo FastH3 Preview has local clip routes; and Comfy’s optimized H3 route broadens local access. No low-cost, independently proven setup delivers continuous context at viewer speed.

catalogue_card.question: Can an “infinite” AI-video broadcast keep the same scene alive?
catalogue_card.text: FastH3 can keep a paced RTMP feed running, but its current project notes say every generated clip hard-cuts. See the queue, fallback, and story boundary before you promise viewers continuity.

summary: Reactor documents a chat-to-queue-to-RTMP FastH3 system, but its model notes say independently generated clips have hard cuts with no continuity of subject, framing, or voice.

The project’s client can automatically chain ready clips and use repeated frames plus silence to keep a 24 fps output clock running. That is delivery continuity, not proof of continuous visual or audio story.

fal’s current H3 Max Director page still describes the closest route to one continuing, directed session, with provider-claimed carried context and hidden overlap. Its public sessions and pricing remain finite and changeable.
Comfy says its optimized H3 path reduces the smallest variants’ total memory footprint to 42.5 GB and supports dynamic-VRAM offloading, but it gives no general speed or hardware-suitability promise.
uncertainty: Reactor’s continuity and timing statements are project-maintainer documentation for one implementation, not independent pool measurements or a viewer study.
fal’s current endpoint terms and continuity behavior are provider claims; a prior provider learning article still conflicts on session and audio details.
Comfy’s memory-optimized H3 statement is not a performance, quality, or minimum-hardware guarantee.
No pool test, invoice, uptime log, end-to-end latency measurement, or first-party pool analytics is available.
freshness_note: Checked 12 September 2026. FastH3 implementation behavior, H3 local compatibility, fal pricing, and session terms can change quickly.
